newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech brewer Plzensky mulls expansion - paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech brewer Plzensky mulls expansion - paper.

text.p: The largest Czech brewing group Plzensky Prazdroj a.s. is interested in increasing its stake in southern brewer Jihoceske Pivovary a.s., economics daily Hospodarske Noviny said on Monday.
The paper quoted Plzensky's chairman Vladimir Perina as saying that Plzensky was interested in increasing its stake in Jihoceske to 40 percent by the year 2000 from the current 22 percent.
He added that Plzensky would consider taking a majority share at a later date.
"In the past days we have sent an official proposal for a capital entry," it quoted Perina as saying.
Perina added that under a plan approved by Plzensky's board, the brewer would first raise its holdings to 30 percent.
Hospodarske said Jihoceske chairman Petr Fencl would welcome the capital expansion as a way of raising funds to pay for new investments and marketing support.
But he added that Jihoceske's owners have not discussed any expansion plan and they would probably not allow Plzensky to take a majority stake in what is the fifth largest domestic brewing group.
"The decision depends on the will of the main shareholders, and an agreement will not be easy," he told the paper.
Officials at both companies were not immediately available for comment.
The main state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund is planning to float 16 percent of Jihoceske shares on the capital market next year.
Bank IPB a.s., Plzensky's biggest private shareholder, also holds 30 percent in Jihoceske together with insurer Ceska Pojistovna's investment arm KIS a.s..

Fencl said a deal with Plzensky could only be done after the government decides on the privatisation of 100 percent state owned brewery Budejovicky Budvar n.p. in which Jihoceske has expressed an interest in taking a stake.

Privatisation of Budvar has been delayed due to a lenghty trademark dispute with the world's largest brewer, U.S.-based Anheuser-Busch. But the Czech Agriculture Ministry has said it will start the sell-off process soon.
The Czech Republic has seen a wave of mergers in the brewing industry, creating several large groups.

Industry experts believe these groups, which apart from Plzensky, Budvar and Jihoceske include Radegast a.s. and Prazske Pivovary a.s. will gradually swallow up most of the country's remaining independent breweries.
